core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 9012-9014): take a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M, a K-injective complex J^bullet representing L, and any complex K^bullet representing K.

Apply the cited composition lemma (proof lines 9015-9024): get a map of complexes from Tot(SheafHom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor SheafHom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet)) to SheafHom^bullet(K^bullet, I^bullet).
Identify these complexes with the derived objects (proof lines 9025-9029): the three displayed complexes represent RSheafHom(L, M), RSheafHom(K, L) and RSheafHom(K, M).

Replace the middle factor by a K-flat representative (proof lines 9030-9047): choosing a K-flat complex H^bullet with a quasi-isomorphism H^bullet -> SheafHom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet) gives a map whose source represents RSheafHom(L, M) tensor^L RSheafHom(K, L).
Compose (proof lines 9047-9049): the composite of the two displayed arrows is the morphism asserted by the lemma.
proof_roadmap: Represent M and L by K-injective complexes and K by an arbitrary complex.
Get the map of internal hom complexes from the earlier composition lemma.
Identify the three internal hom complexes with the corresponding RSheafHom objects.
Resolve the middle factor by a K-flat complex so that the tensor product computes the derived tensor product.
Compose the two arrows to obtain the asserted canonical morphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the composition morphism for RSheafHom on a ringed site, from the derived tensor product of RSheafHom(L, M) and RSheafHom(K, L) to RSheafHom(K, M) (statement lines 8997-9008). The construction needs three competing representative choices at once: M and L must be represented by K-injective complexes so that the internal hom complexes compute RSheafHom, while the middle factor has to be replaced by a K-flat representative so that the tensor product computes the derived tensor product, and only then can the two displayed arrows be composed (proof lines 9012-9047). The non-formal point is exactly this bookkeeping, which the author spells out. The claim is H2: one construction whose input is a choice of resolutions, with the omitted functoriality not being part of the counted assertion.
